ledger.claim: The deviation is established on this trip's own measurements. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure, and the trace measures 30.89 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against the platform's optimal estimate of 22.10 km stored on the trip record. Excess = 8.79 km, or 39.8% of optimal. Both establishment gates in POL-RD-01 pass: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, so no threshold straddle is in play here and the trace figure is the one cited.

The excess is additionally a MATERIAL deviation under POL-RD-01: 8.79 km exceeds the 8.0 km absolute materiality gate. The two limbs of the materiality test are alternatives, so the fact that 39.8% falls short of the 50% limb does not matter. Materiality is what triggers the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check, and it is assessed on the excess remaining after any POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 adjustment — none of which is available to the driver here.

The trip record's 30.9 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test; the trace's 30.89 km governs under POL-RD-01. Nothing outcome-changing turns on the difference in this case, because both figures clear both gates, but the correct excess denominator is the trace figure and the correct excess is 8.79 km, not the 8.8 km the rounded field would suggest.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes and needs no corroboration. It carries 217 fixes at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage, an empty gaps array, a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds and a sustained sampling interval of 10 seconds. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met — there is no gap above 90 seconds, no straight-line jump above 500 m and no sampling interval above 30 seconds — so the trace carries the establishment finding on its own and no escalation arises under POL-RD-10(3).

The driver's fog explanation is unsupported by anything in the pool. POL-RD-03 exonerates a deviation only against a traffic_advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached that segment, and is matched by a route that leaves and rejoins the optimal corridor. No such advisory exists: EV-ADVIS-00505-01 is MISSING, its payload is null, and it carries admissibility weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING, detail: no advisory covers the SLE or TPE in this window). I disclose that impairment expressly: this artifact can prove nothing by its content, but its absence is itself citable, and it leaves condition (a) of POL-RD-03 unmet, so the clause cannot exonerate the 8.79 km.

The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden and it has shifted to the driver. Trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00505; the trace runs from the recorded start at 05:46:40 to the recorded end at 06:22:40 with no timestamp disagreement, and the excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The driver must therefore point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. His counterparty statement does not deny the route — it explains it ('I went around') — and its reason is a fog assertion naming no traffic_advisory ID, no closed road and no gantry. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge that burden, and assertions citing no evidence ID carry no weight.

No rider-requested detour can be made out under POL-RD-04. The chat log for this trip contains 0 messages, with first_message_at and last_message_at both null and message_count 0, so there is no rider instruction, no timestamp to test against the departure from the optimal corridor, no named road, and no waypoint_hint field for the 200 m corroboration test. The clause's corroboration limb is not even reachable, and POL-RD-04 offers the driver no exoneration.

POL-RD-05 cannot be run. Pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on the trip record, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null with them. There is therefore no stored re-quote against which POL-RD-01 could be re-applied between amended endpoints, and no basis for substituting any other optimal figure. The dropoff label ('Changi Airport Terminal 1, Arrival Pick-up Bay 3') carries venue_id null and sits under an amendment field the record never stamped; the clause requires an amendment, not an amended-sounding bay label.

The pooled-itinerary baseline in POL-RD-12 does not apply. The vehicle type on this trip is RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so the 22.10 km figure is the ordinary platform optimal computed at booking and is the correct comparator under POL-RD-01. There is no matched-itinerary optimal for the driver to point to, and no co-rider distance to exclude.

The figure is also well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so no de minimis disposal is available to the driver.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The route question is settled by the GPS trace, not by the trip record's rounded copy. EV-GPS-00505 measures 30.89 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff; the platform's optimal estimate stored on EV-TRIP-00505 is 22.10 km. The excess is 8.79 km, or 39.8% of optimal, which clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and also the 8.0 km absolute gate, so this is a MATERIAL deviation. The trace is complete — 217 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and no jump — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07, nothing need corroborate it, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. The driver's own statement ('I went around') does not dispute the route. The driver's fog account does not excuse the deviation. POL-RD-03 exonerates only against a traffic advisory naming a road the optimal route uses, with a window covering the trip. The only advisory in the record is EV-ADVIS-00505-01, which is MISSING — no payload, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — and it records that no advisory covered the SLE or TPE in that window. The driver produced no advisory ID and no artifact of his own, so POL-RD-08 applies: a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the burden that shifts to the driver once the rider has shown a qualifying excess on an unimpaired trace. The fog assertion is discarded and the excess stands. I have considered, and do not adopt, the submission that this record must be escalated under POL-RD-10(5). That trigger covers an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool, does not cover the trip window, or lacks the field the clause requires. Here the driver cited no artifact and invoked no clause in reliance on one; the record is not missing a document it should hold (LTA issued no advisory for that corridor and window, as the mined artifact itself records), so the POL-RD-03 test is not untestable — it runs and fails. That is a failure of the driver's proof, which POL-RD-08 resolves, not a broken or incomplete record of the kind POL-RD-10 holds. The refund is arithmetic. The fare is METERED on EV-FARE-00505, so POL-RD-02 governs and the upfront-quote route in POL-RD-11 does not. Recomputing on the optimal route: ((3.80 base fare + 0.75 × 22.10 km + 0.28 × 27.0 min) × surge 1.0, read from the fare breakdown's own surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 28.735. Charged total was 37.86. Refund = 37.86 − 28.735 = 9.125, rounded up to SGD 9.15. That is 24.2% of the charge, well below the 90% that would make it a full refund and well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. No other money moves. There is no off-route ERP, toll or surcharge line to correct (all nil), so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and its anti-double-count rule keeps the distance refund clean. The driver's trailing-90-day record (0 deviation flags in 250 completed trips) establishes no POL-RD-06 pattern, so there is no full-refund uplift and no conduct referral. The chat log is empty, so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04; no amendment is stamped, so POL-RD-05 does not run; the vehicle is RYDE_PLUS, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The SGD 210 rebooking cost and the missed check-in are not remedies this policy provides and no clause turns them into a refundable line; the contested sum is the 37.86 charged. Profile fields other than the two trailing-90-day counters POL-RD-06 names (and the POL-RD-08 rider counters, which are not engaged) are context only under POL-GEN-01 — the driver's 4.86 rating, account age, lifetime trips and lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter, and the rider's own profile — and I have used none of them as a ground. The counterparty statement is evidence, but it carries no weight multiplier and does not enter or move the confidence cap. Confidence is 0.90: the deciding facts are carried by artifacts each at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-00505, EV-TRIP-00505, EV-FARE-00505), so nothing caps it below the floor.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
